audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker was described as a flat pull-stun. Riot's text: it stuns only if enemies are on opposite sides of Sett; enemies on one side are slowed instead.
audit.why: That is the decisive positioning rule of the lane — keeping the minion wave behind you downgrades his engage to a slow, which is exactly what a 675-range enchanter needs.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns with the 16s rank-1 cooldown, plus Haymaker's 18s cooldown and its true-damage centre (shield absorbs it, MR does not).

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere in the cooldown section.

edits.before: Q poke at level 1 is among the best in the game — chunk Sett on every last-hit and start the Mantra economy.
edits.after: Mantra is usable at level 1 — open RQ Soulflare and chunk Sett while his Grit bar is empty and worth nothing.

edits.before: Full kit: E shield-speed makes you untouchable in short trades. Mantra-Q (RQ) on cooldown gaps is a third of his HP.
edits.after: Grit takes over: a charged Haymaker shields him and hits true damage through the middle — refuse the long trade.

edits.before: Spam the RQ slow-field on his farming spots and keep your shield for Facebreaker — the lane is a toll booth and you own it.
edits.after: His bullying peak — double punches plus a stored Haymaker out-trade you the moment your one Inspire shield is on its 9s cooldown.

edits.before: First item amplifies the RQ chunk — keep him under 60% and the lane stays yours by default.
edits.after: He can Facebreaker, R and Haymaker before your shield matters — the point-blank duel is his.

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: Your item resharpens RQ, but he scales into a tanky bruiser — a coinflip you only win off the map.

edits.before: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: 16s at rank 1, and it only stuns if he catches enemies on both sides of him — keep the minions behind you and it is a slow. Step up on its downtime. - Haymaker is 18s at rank 1 and its centre is true damage: your shield eats it, your MR does not.

notes: The content whys for this matchup were already accurate and even state their own side in plain words ('so the first level is Karma's', 'the late read is Skill') — the chart sides simply did not match them, in both layers. Facebreaker's stun requiring enemies on opposite sides was absent everywhere and is the single most useful positioning fact in the lane. Sett's W tooltip range of 25000 in the kit file is a parsing artifact, not a real range.
